The slider that steps through an iterative method belongs **above the chart**, not in the panel with the problem's inputs -- it's what the reader scrubs while watching. `ojs-chart-controls` puts it there and keeps it there in fullscreen; the playback module gives it a ▶; and because `layout()` reads the sweep's pace, the chart tweens smoothly from one iterate to the next.

```{ojs}
VM = window.VM
vmTheme = Generators.observe(notify => VM.plotting.onThemeChange(notify))
chartColors = VM.plotting.colors(vmTheme)
```

## Inputs

::: {.ojs-panel .ojs-row}
```{ojs}
viewof newtonF = Inputs.text({label: "f(x)", value: "cos(x) - x"})
```
```{ojs}
viewof newtonX0 = Inputs.text({label: "x₀", value: "3"})
```
```{ojs}
viewof newtonMax = Inputs.text({label: "max iterations", value: "12"})
```
:::

## All the iterates, computed once

Compute the whole sequence in one cell; the slider then only chooses how many to *show*. This keeps the slider cell cheap (it re-runs on every tick of a sweep) and makes the table trivial.

```{ojs}
iterates = {
  const f = VM.expressions.makeFunction(math, newtonF)
  const df = VM.expressions.makeDerivative(math, newtonF)
  const x0 = VM.expressions.makeNumber(math, newtonX0)
  const max = VM.expressions.makeNumber(math, newtonMax)
  if (f === null || df === null || x0 === null || max === null) return null
  const xs = [x0]
  for (let n = 0; n < Math.min(max, 60); n++) {
    const x = xs[xs.length - 1]
    const d = df(x)
    if (!Number.isFinite(d) || d === 0) break
    const next = x - f(x) / d
    if (!Number.isFinite(next)) break
    xs.push(next)
  }
  return {f, xs}
}
```

## The chart block

The slider's range depends on how many iterates exist, so its `viewof` is **recreated** whenever `iterates` changes -- which is exactly the situation `applyExampleParams` warns about, and why that function takes selectors. Nothing to do here; just be aware the element isn't stable.

::: {.ojs-chart-block}
::: {.ojs-chart-controls}
```{ojs}
viewof step = Inputs.range([0, iterates ? iterates.xs.length - 1 : 0], {label: "iteration n", step: 1, value: 0})
```
:::
```{ojs}
mainPlot = {
  const data = []
  if (iterates !== null) {
    const {f, xs} = iterates
    const shown = xs.slice(0, step + 1)
    const range = VM.plotting.paddedRange(shown, {minPadding: 1})
    const cx = [], cy = []
    for (let i = 0; i <= 300; i++) { const x = range.lo + (range.hi - range.lo) * i / 300; cx.push(x); cy.push(f(x)) }
    data.push({x: cx, y: cy, name: "f(x)", line: {color: chartColors.fn, width: 2.5}})
    // Tangent from the current iterate to the next: the picture of one Newton step.
    if (step < xs.length - 1) {
      const x = xs[step]
      data.push({x: [x, xs[step + 1]], y: [f(x), 0], name: "tangent", line: {color: chartColors.alt, width: 1.5, dash: "dot"}})
    }
    const labels = []
    for (let n = 0; n <= step; n++) labels.push("x" + VM.plotting.subscript(n))
    data.push({x: shown, y: shown.map(() => 0), mode: "markers+text", text: labels, textposition: "bottom center", name: "iterates",
      marker: {color: chartColors.muted, size: 8, line: {color: chartColors.halo, width: 1.5}}})
    data.push({x: [xs[step]], y: [f(xs[step])], mode: "markers", name: "current", marker: {color: chartColors.ok, size: 12, line: {color: chartColors.halo, width: 2}}})
  }
  const div = document.createElement("div")
  div.className = "plotly-box-large"
  div.style.height = "400px"; div.style.minHeight = "0"
  Plotly.newPlot(div, data, VM.plotting.layout({
    showlegend: false,
    xaxis: {title: "x"},
    yaxis: {zeroline: true},
    annotations: iterates ? [] : VM.plotting.emptyState("Check the inputs")
  }), VM.plotting.config())
  VM.plotting.autoResize(div)
  return div
}
```
:::

Press ▶. The tween length comes from `VM.ui.playbackTweenMs`, which the playback module publishes and `layout()` reads -- so at 4× the chart still lands each frame before the next arrives, instead of a fixed 300 ms tween being cut off every time.

## The table

`renderTable` takes header cells that may be KaTeX nodes (`tex` is an OJS global) and separate plain-text headers for the CSV.

```{ojs}
{
  if (iterates === null) return html`<em>No iterates.</em>`
  const rows = []
  for (let n = 0; n <= step; n++) {
    const x = iterates.xs[n]
    rows.push([n, x.toPrecision(10), Math.abs(iterates.f(x)).toExponential(3)])
  }
  return VM.ui.renderTable({html, headers: ["n", tex`x_n`, tex`|f(x_n)|`], rows, csvHeaders: ["n", "x_n", "|f(x_n)|"], filename: "newton-iterates.csv"})
}
```
